previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, and chronic venous thromboembolism was admitted for dyspnea on exertion and significant weight gain. She was found to have pulmonary edema due to volume overload, a subtherapeutic INR from discontinued warfarin, and a urinary tract infection with E. coli and Enterococcus. She was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral furosemide, and bridged with heparin before resuming warfarin. A CT scan revealed findings suggestive of sarcoidosis, prompting a pulmonary referral. She developed transient hyperkalemia, likely due to heparin-induced hyperaldosteronism, and experienced lightheadedness from volume shifts, managed with physical therapy. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to extended care with follow-up plans for sarcoidosis, iron deficiency anemia, and anticoagulation management.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Chest, single AP upright portable view.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with history of shortness of breath,
cardiomyopathy.

___ and ___.

FINDINGS:  AP upright portable views of the chest were obtained.  The exam is
suboptimal due to underpenetration from patient body habitus.  Given this, the
cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are grossly stable.  Prominence of the
interstitial markings bilaterally is most consistent with mild interstitial
edema.  No lobar consolidation is seen.  There is no large pleural effusion or
pneumothorax.

HISTORY:  ___ female with history of interstitial lung disease
(possible sarcoidosis on prior chest CT) and congestive heart failure, now
presenting with shortness of breath and cough.

COMPARISON:  Portable chest radiograph from ___ and CTA of the
chest from ___.

PORTABLE SEMI-ERECT FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  Re-demonstrated is unchanged
moderate interstitial pulmonary edema superimposed upon patient's underlying
chronic lung disease.  Overall increased density of the lung bases is likely
secondary to attenuation artifact due to the patient's body habitus.  No
confluent consolidation is identified.  There is no pneumothorax. 
Cardiomediastinal and hilar contours remain mildly enlarged, though unchanged
from prior.

IMPRESSION:  Persistent moderate interstitial pulmonary edema.
